comparisons.peer_topic: Corporate Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting Obligations
comparisons.peer_summary: Evolving expectations and laws regarding corporate responsibility, including climate data reporting and third-party verification (e.g., in California), may impose additional compliance costs, require costly supply chain modifications, and result in reputational or financial harm if AMD fails to comply or meet stakeholder expectations.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose that regulatory non-compliance can lead to significant compliance costs and reputational harm. However, AMD specifically highlights evolving corporate responsibility and climate data reporting requirements (e.g., in California) as a driver for these costs and the need for third-party verification, whereas MU's disclosure is broader, focusing on general laws, regulations, and industry standards affecting its third-party sales channel partners, explicitly listing suspension of production or sales as a key risk alongside penalties.

sentences.text: • suspension of production or sales of our products;
• increased compliance costs;
• reputational challenges.

Compliance with, or our failure, or the failure of our third-party sales channel partners or agents, to comply with, laws, regulations, or industry standards could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, or financial condition.

As the nature, scope and complexity of corporate responsibility reporting and disclosure requirements continue to evolve, we may incur additional compliance costs and indirect compliance costs from our customers and, suppliers that are passed on to us.

For example, the state of California has passed reporting requirements that will require corporations to report on climate data and these laws include data assurance requirements that entail third-party verifications.

Our failure to comply, or the appearance of our failure to comply, with these legal and regulatory requirements can result in regulatory penalties, fines and legal liabilities, increase costs, and harm our reputation - any of which could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operation.

comparisons.peer_topic: Semiconductor manufacturing and distribution regulatory compliance
comparisons.peer_summary: Compliance with technical standards and laws regarding hazardous materials and environmental impact in semiconductor manufacturing increases design and procurement costs, may require process modifications or product re-engineering, and failure to comply could result in litigation, fines, and distribution disruptions.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies face risks from non-compliance with laws and regulations governing their manufacturing and distribution activities. Similar to MU, which risks suspension of production or sales, AVGO discloses that failure to comply with technical standards and hazardous material laws could lead to litigation, fines, and specifically requiring them to 'stop distributing our products commercially until they comply' or re-engineer products. Both identify increased costs as a shared consequence of compliance efforts.

sentences.text: • suspension of production or sales of our products;
• increased compliance costs;
• regulatory penalties, fines, civil or criminal sanctions, and other legal liabilities; and

We must comply with technical standards and a variety of domestic and international laws and regulations in the manufacture and distribution of our semiconductors, the costs of which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

This could increase the complexity and costs of our product design and procurement operations, require us to stop distributing our products commercially until they comply with such new standards, lead our customers to suspend imports of their products into that country, require us to re-engineer our products and disrupt cross-border manufacturing relationships.
Any failure by us to comply with such requirements could result in litigation against us and the payment of significant fines and damages by us in the event of a significant adverse judgment.

comparisons.peer_topic: Risks associated with environmental, health, safety, and product regulations
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel is subject to complex and evolving environmental, health, and safety laws governing its manufacturing materials and supplier operations. Non-compliance by Intel or its suppliers can lead to regulatory penalties, production suspensions, increased costs, and reputational damage. Specific regulations regarding hazardous materials, greenhouse gas emissions (such as perfluorocarbons), and PFAS chemicals may require additional abatement equipment, process alterations, or reliance on limited alternatives, potentially increasing manufacturing costs as capacity expands.
comparisons.comparison: There is a strong factual overlap in the consequences of regulatory non-compliance between MU and INTC. Both companies explicitly list 'suspension of production' and 'regulatory penalties, fines, and legal liabilities' as direct outcomes of failing to comply with evolving laws. Both also emphasize the role of suppliers in this risk; MU warns of failure by 'third-party sales channel partners or agents,' while INTC highlights that 'failure or inability to comply by our suppliers' can require suspension of production processes. INTC further details that environmental regulations may require 'additional remediation obligations' and 'alteration' of manufacturing processes.

sentences.text: • suspension of production or sales of our products;
• increased compliance costs;
• regulatory penalties, fines, civil or criminal sanctions, and other legal liabilities; and
• reputational challenges.

Compliance with, or our failure, or the failure of our third-party sales channel partners or agents, to comply with, laws, regulations, or industry standards could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations, or financial condition.

The amendment or expansion of these laws or regulations, as well as our failure or inability to comply with them (including as a result of acquired entities), can result in regulatory penalties, fines, and legal liabilities; increased costs; additional remediation obligations; suspension of production; alteration, suspension, or termination of our manufacturing and assembly and test processes, including due to an inability to find, afford, or attain adequate substitute materials, equipment, or processes; damage to our reputation; and restrictions on our operations or sales.
In addition, the failure or inability to comply by our suppliers of these materials can require us to suspend or alter our production processes and sources, and result in increased risks and costs.

comparisons.peer_topic: Environmental and Climate Change Compliance and Physical Risks
comparisons.peer_summary: The company faces risks from complex and evolving environmental laws leading to compliance costs and liabilities for contamination, as well as risks from climate change that may drive new regulations increasing costs and cause physical disruptions to facilities and operations.
comparisons.comparison: MU and QCOM share specific overlapping consequences for regulatory non-compliance, particularly 'suspension of production,' 'regulatory penalties, fines and legal liabilities,' and 'damage to our reputation.' Both disclosures also link these risks to complex and evolving environmental laws. However, QCOM's disclosure expands on the physical aspect by including 'alteration of our manufacturing, assembly or test processes' and restrictions on facility modification/expansion, whereas MU's disclosure broadly covers 'industry standards' and includes risks related to third-party sales channel partners.
